markdown_file: Europe/Isle of Man (Manx people)/013 - The Lhondoo And The Ushag-Reaisht.md

segments.source: One time Lhondoo, the Blackbird, was living in the mountains and Ushag-reaisht, the Bird of the Waste, as Manx ones call the Golden Plover, was living in the lowlands, and neither of them was able to leave his own haunts.
One day, however, the two birds met on the borders between mountain and plain, and they made it up between them that they would change places for a while.
The Bird of the Waste should stay in the mountains till the Lhondoo should return.
The Lhondoo found himself better off in his new home than in the old one, and he did not go back.
So the poor Bird of the Waste was left in the mountains and any day you may hear him cry in a mournful voice:
‘Lhondoo, vel oo cheet, vel oo cheet?
Black Thrush, are you coming, are you coming?
The time is long and you are not here!
‘Cha jig dy braa, cha jig dy braa!’
Will never come, will never come!
It’s very cold, it’s very cold.
Then the Blackbird goes his ways.
